{{Short description|Special kind of adjunction between categories named after Daniel Quillen}}
In [[homotopy theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''Quillen adjunction''' between two [[closed model category|closed model categories]] '''C''' and '''D''' is a special kind of [[adjoint functor|adjunction]] between [[category (mathematics)|categories]] that induces an adjunction between the [[homotopy category|homotopy categories]] Ho('''C''') and Ho('''D''') via the [[total derived functor]] construction. Quillen adjunctions are named in honor of the mathematician [[Daniel Quillen]].

==Formal definition==
Given two closed model categories '''C''' and '''D''', a '''Quillen adjunction''' is a pair
:(''F'', ''G''): '''C''' <math>\leftrightarrows</math> '''D'''
of [[adjoint functor]]s with ''F'' left adjoint to ''G'' such that ''F'' preserves [[cofibration]]s and trivial cofibrations or, equivalently by the closed model axioms, such that ''G'' preserves [[fibration]]s and trivial fibrations. In such an adjunction ''F'' is called the '''left Quillen functor''' and ''G'' is called the '''right Quillen functor'''.

==Properties==
It is a consequence of the axioms that a left (right) Quillen functor preserves [[weak equivalence (homotopy theory)|weak equivalence]]s between cofibrant (fibrant) objects. The [[total derived functor theorem]] of Quillen says that the total left derived functor
:'''L'''''F'': Ho('''C''') &rarr; Ho('''D''')
is a left adjoint to the total right derived functor
:'''R'''''G'': Ho('''D''') &rarr; Ho('''C''').
This adjunction ('''L'''''F'', '''R'''''G'') is called the '''derived adjunction'''.

If (''F'', ''G'') is a Quillen adjunction as above such that
:''F''(''c'') &rarr; ''d''
with ''c'' cofibrant and ''d'' fibrant is a weak equivalence in '''D''' if and only if
:''c'' &rarr; ''G''(''d'')
is a weak equivalence in '''C''' then it is called a '''Quillen equivalence''' of the closed model categories '''C''' and '''D'''. In this case the derived adjunction is an adjoint [[equivalence of categories]] so that
:'''L'''''F''(''c'') &rarr; ''d''
is an isomorphism in Ho('''D''') if and only if 
:''c'' &rarr; '''R'''''G''(''d'')
is an isomorphism in Ho('''C''').
